arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01, initiated via a phishing email that triggered an encoded PowerShell command from Outlook. This led to the execution of a malicious DLL through rundll32.exe from the user's Temp directory, establishing C2 communication over HTTPS to a known-bad external IP. The attacker performed reconnaissance and lateral movement activities. Initial detection was delayed due to lack of behavioral correlation rules. Response actions were denied due to procedural gaps in authorization protocols.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 conducted Nmap SYN scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Alert generated but not escalated (low severity).
Successful internal authentication from WS-IT-101 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) by CORP\helpdesk account.
User CORP\jsmith launched Outlook on WS-FIN-AP01.
Encoded PowerShell command executed under user context, spawned by outlook.exe (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned DLL from %TEMP% directory, beaconing to 198.51.100.23:443 (T1218.011, T1071.001). Hosts file modification detected (T1565.001).
Incident detected and investigation initiated based on EDR alerts.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine) attempted but denied due to authorization and targeting issues.

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Office Application
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
    Image|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  condition: selection
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
description: Detects encoded PowerShell launched from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

rule Malicious_Dll_Loading_Via_Rundll32_From_Temp {
    meta:
        description = "Detects rundll32 loading DLL from user temp directory"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        date = "2026-04-12"
    strings:
        $s1 = "\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\" fullword ascii
        $s2 = "rundll32.exe" fullword ascii
    condition:
        $s1 and $s2
}

arguments.summary: A critical lateral movement incident was detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which conducted a network scan against internal host WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). The scan triggered a low-severity alert but was not escalated. Subsequent authentication activity from the compromised host to the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet indicates potential lateral movement. Despite detection, containment actions (firewall block, endpoint quarantine) were denied due to approval and parameter errors, highlighting process gaps in incident response.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 initiated a SYN scan against 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected by IDS as 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan'. Alert severity: low.
Successful internal authentication from 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) to 10.0.1.1 using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
UEBA analysis shows svc_backup account exhibiting low-risk behavioral anomalies (slightly elevated file access).
SIEM correlation identifies link between external scan and internal authentication. Lateral movement suspected.
Containment actions (firewall block, EPP quarantine, IAM disable, Ansible remediation) attempted but denied due to approval and parameter issues.

title: Suspicious External to Internal Scan Followed by Authentication
logsource:
  category: firewall
  product: generic

  scan_event:
    event_type: network_scan
    src_ip|cidr: '0.0.0.0/0'

  auth_event:

    src_ip: scan_event.dst_ip
    user: '*'
  timeframe: 2h
condition: scan_event and auth_event
level: high

rule PotentialLateralMovementProcess {
    meta:
        description = "Detects common tools used in lateral movement"
        author = "SOC Team"
        date = "2026-04-19"
    strings:
        $smb_exec = "net use \\* \\ipc$" wide ascii
        $psexec = "psexec" wide ascii nocase
        $wmi_remote = "wmic /node:*" wide ascii
    condition:
        any of them
}
